hero.title: How much does SEO cost in Portugal in 2026?
hero.intro: SEO doesn't have a single price — it depends on the current state of your website, competition in your sector and the level of support you're looking for. In this guide we explain what influences cost, how to compare proposals and how much to invest in a professional SEO strategy in Portugal, with Artecium's real plans.

sections.title: What influences SEO pricing?
paragraphs: SEO cost depends less on "how many keywords you want to rank for" and more on the starting point: a technically solid website with clear content requires less initial work than a slow, poorly structured site with little relevant content.

Other factors include the sector (more competition means more effort), the number of languages or markets, the need for new content regularly and whether SEO is local, national or targeted at specific markets.

That's why very generic proposals or fixed prices without understanding the project context are usually a red flag. A good SEO provider starts by understanding the website, business goals and what's already been done before defining the investment.

sections.title: What does SEO typically include?
sections.intro: Depending on the plan, professional SEO can cover several areas — not all are needed from day one.
items: Technical audit: speed, indexing, URL structure, metadata and errors that prevent Google from reading the site correctly
Keyword research and search intent aligned with the company's services
On-page optimisation: titles, descriptions, headings and internal linking between pages
Content: creation or review of search-oriented and conversion-focused copy
Local SEO: Google Business Profile, citations and NAP consistency (name, address, phone)
Reporting: tracking positions, organic traffic and progress over time
GEO / AI Search: optimisation for answer engines and presence in AI-generated results

At Artecium, website plans include basic technical best practices (structure, performance, essential metadata). Ongoing SEO — research, optimised content and monitoring — is a complementary service, from €350 (Foundation) or on monthly plans.

If you don't have a website yet or are planning a redesign, it's worth thinking about both investments together. A professional site from €750 (Essential) with SEO Foundation can be a solid starting point for many businesses.

hero.title: Professional website vs cheap website — what actually changes?
hero.intro: Cheap websites exist for a reason — and so do professional ones. The question isn't which is "better" in abstract, but which makes sense for your business, goals and time horizon. We compare both objectively, without alarmism or empty promises.

sections.title: Why do prices vary so much?
paragraphs: A website can cost €200 or €2,000 — and in both cases someone will say they deliver "a website". The difference is in what's included: design time, code quality, search engine optimisation, device testing, form setup, deployment and what happens after launch.

Very cheap solutions usually rely on generic templates with minimal customisation and no follow-up. Professional websites involve business analysis, content structure designed for conversion, performance and preparation to evolve.
At Artecium, websites start at €750 (Essential) — not because it's the minimum possible, but because it reflects the work needed to deliver a solid, fast site ready to grow.

sections.title: Side-by-side comparison
sections.intro: This table summarises common differences — details vary by provider, but patterns are consistent in the market.

rows.col2: Design aligned with the brand, consistent typography and colours
Optimised for speed; tested on mobile and desktop

rows.col1: Basic or missing metadata; weak structure
rows.col2: Structure, headings, metadata and indexing configured
Content structure designed for the business and conversion

sections.title: Hidden costs of cheap websites
sections.intro: A low initial price can hide expenses or limitations that only appear later.

items.title: Rework
items.description: A poorly built site may need to be redone in 1–2 years — doubling the investment. Rebuilding is usually more expensive than doing it right from the start.

items.title: No SEO
items.description: Without a technical SEO foundation, the website may never appear in relevant search results — meaning the online presence investment generates no return.

items.title: Vendor dependency
items.description: Closed platforms or proprietary builders can make it hard to migrate the site or make changes independently.

items.title: Security and updates
items.description: Websites without maintenance accumulate vulnerabilities. Security issues can affect company reputation and visitor trust.

sections.title: When a cheap website may be enough
sections.intro: Being honest also means recognising scenarios where minimum investment makes sense.
items: Quick validation of an idea or one-off campaign (temporary landing page)
Minimal online presence with no expectation of generating organic leads
Very limited budget with a clear plan to evolve later
Personal project or portfolio with no commercial component

sections.title: When to invest in a professional website
paragraphs: If the website is the main channel for credibility and contact for your business, investing in a professional site tends to pay off. Service companies, clinics, consultants, local shops and B2B businesses benefit from a site that conveys trust, loads fast and appears when someone searches for what they offer.

At Artecium, the Essential plan (€750) covers the solid online presence most small and medium businesses need. Professional (€1,500) adds content depth, SEO structure and conversion preparation. Business projects (from €2,500) include advanced features, integrations or specific requirements.
The decision isn't "cheap vs expensive" — it's "what does my business need now and in two years?".

sections.title: How to compare proposals objectively
paragraphs: Always ask for detail on what's included: number of pages, design revisions, SEO setup, forms, deployment, domain, hosting and what happens after launch. Two proposals at different prices may include completely different scopes.
Also ask about code ownership, ability to evolve the site and who handles maintenance. A professional website should be an asset the company controls — not a permanent dependency on an opaque vendor.

items.question: Is a €750 website professional?
items.answer: Yes. At Artecium, the Essential plan (€750) includes custom design, clear structure, contact form, basic optimisation and deployment. It's a professional website for businesses that need a solid presence without advanced features.

items.question: Do cheap websites appear on Google?
items.answer: They can be indexed, but without adequate technical SEO, relevant content and performance, it's unlikely they'll appear in useful positions for competitive keywords. Appearing on Google and being found by potential clients are different things.

items.question: Can I start cheap and evolve later?
items.answer: Yes, but it's worth planning that evolution. Migrating from a generic builder to a professional website may involve rework. If you know you'll need SEO, a blog or integrations, it makes sense to start on a base that supports that.

items.question: What's the difference between Essential and Professional?
items.answer: Essential (€750) focuses on a clear, professional online presence. Professional (€1,500) adds more content depth, SEO structure, dedicated service sections and better preparation for conversion and growth.

items.question: Is it worth paying more for custom design?
items.answer: It depends on the sector and competition. For businesses where visual trust is decisive — healthcare, consulting, premium services — a generic design can convey lack of professionalism. For quick validation, a template may suffice temporarily.

hero.title: What is SEO and why does it matter?
hero.intro: SEO — Search Engine Optimization — is the set of practices that help a website be found in search engines like Google. For businesses in Portugal, it's often the most sustainable way to generate visibility and leads online. We explain the essentials, without unnecessary jargon.

sections.title: What is SEO, really?
paragraphs: SEO means optimising a website so search engines understand it, index it correctly and show it to people searching for what the company offers. It's not a trick or secret formula — it's consistent work across three areas: technical, content and authority.

When someone searches "lawyer in Lisbon" or "website development Portugal", Google decides which pages to show based on hundreds of factors. SEO is the work of ensuring your website meets the relevant criteria to appear in those searches.
It's important to distinguish SEO from paid advertising: Google ads appear while you pay; SEO builds organic visibility that persists over time.

sections.title: The three pillars of SEO
sections.intro: Modern SEO rests on three complementary areas — neglecting any of them limits results.

items.title: Technical SEO
items.description: Site speed, URL structure, indexing, metadata, mobile compatibility and absence of errors that prevent Google from reading content. It's the foundation — without it, the rest has little effect.

items.title: Content
items.description: Copy, titles and pages that answer the questions potential clients ask. Relevant, clear and well-structured content is what Google wants to show in results.

items.title: Authority
items.description: Signals that the website is a credible reference in its sector — links from other sites, mentions, consistent local presence and online reputation.

sections.title: Why does SEO matter for businesses?
sections.intro: For most service companies and local businesses, Google is where clients start searching.
items: Organic visibility: appearing in results without paying for each click
Credibility: businesses that appear at the top are perceived as more relevant
Qualified traffic: someone searching "service X" has intent — it's not random traffic
Long-term cost: the investment accumulates; it doesn't depend on continuous ad budget
Website complement: a professional site without SEO is like a shop without a sign on the main street

sections.title: What to expect from SEO — realistically
paragraphs: SEO doesn't produce overnight results. Depending on the sector, competition and current website state, it can take weeks or months to see significant progress in positions and organic traffic.
It's also not a guarantee of #1 position for all keywords. The realistic goal is to appear on the first pages for terms relevant to the business — and improve progressively over time.

SEO works best as a continuous investment, not a one-off action. An initial technical setup (like Artecium's SEO Foundation at €350) prepares the base; monthly support (Growth at €400/month or Advanced at €750/month) maintains and accelerates growth.

sections.title: Local SEO — especially relevant in Portugal
sections.intro: For businesses serving clients in a geographic area, local SEO is often the most impactful starting point.
items: Google Business Profile optimisation (formerly Google My Business)
Consistency of name, address and phone across directories and the website
Service pages with geographic reference (e.g. "SEO in Lisbon")
Reviews and presence on relevant local platforms
Content that answers searches with local intent

sections.title: SEO starts with the website
paragraphs: It doesn't make sense to invest in SEO on a poorly built website. Slow speed, confusing structure, insufficient content or technical errors limit what any strategy can achieve.

That's why SEO and website should be thought of together. At Artecium, website plans (from €750) include basic technical best practices. Ongoing SEO is a complementary service that maximises the return on that initial investment.

items.question: SEO or Google Ads — which to choose?
items.answer: They're complementary, not mutually exclusive. Google Ads generates immediate traffic while you pay; SEO builds organic visibility in the medium term. Many businesses start with SEO Foundation and consider ads for one-off campaigns.

items.question: Do I need SEO if I have social media?
items.answer: Yes. Social media and SEO serve different audiences. Many people search on Google before contacting a business — especially for local services or B2B. Ignoring SEO means missing that audience.

items.question: How long does SEO take to work?
items.answer: It depends on the sector and starting point. Technical improvements may reflect in weeks; consistent growth in positions and organic traffic usually takes 3–6 months or more. SEO is a medium-term investment.

items.question: What is GEO / AI Search?
items.answer: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) refers to optimisation for answer engines and AI-generated results — like Google AI Overview or ChatGPT responses. It's an evolution of traditional SEO, included in Artecium's SEO Advanced plan.

items.question: Can I do SEO myself?
items.answer: Some basics — metadata, clear content, Google Business Profile — you can handle internally. Technical SEO, keyword research, content strategy and competitor analysis benefit from professional experience, especially in competitive sectors.

hero.title: Website or web application — which do you need?
hero.intro: Not every online project is a website — and not every business needs a web application. Confusing the two leads to wrong investments: paying too much for unnecessary features or ending up with a site that doesn't support what the business needs. We explain the differences practically.

sections.title: Website vs web application — simple definitions
paragraphs: A website is essentially informational: it presents the company, services, contact methods and relevant content. The visitor reads, browses and contacts — they don't interact with complex business logic.

A web application involves continuous interaction, authentication (login), dashboards, internal processes or features that go beyond displaying information. Examples: client portal, order management, internal team tool, booking system with advanced logic.

The boundary isn't always rigid — a professional website can include advanced forms, simple restricted areas or integrations. But when business logic is central, we're probably talking about a web application.

sections.title: When a website is enough
sections.intro: These scenarios are solved with a professional website — no web application needed.

items.title: Lead capture
items.description: Forms, landing pages and conversion-oriented structure — still within the scope of a website.

items.title: Blog and content for SEO
items.description: Publish articles, guides and service pages to improve visibility in search engines.

items.title: Simple integrations
items.description: Newsletter, basic CRM, chatbot or contact automation — possible on a Business website (from €2,500) without being a full app.

sections.title: When you need a web application
sections.intro: These scenarios require business logic, authentication or data processing — beyond a traditional website.

items.title: Client portal
items.description: Clients log in to view orders, documents, invoices or service status.

items.title: Internal tool
items.description: Dashboard for the team to manage requests, inventory, projects or internal processes.

items.title: Complex booking platform
items.description: System with availability, payments, automatic confirmations and user management.

items.title: Digital product
items.description: SaaS, marketplace or online tool that is the business's own product.

sections.title: How much does each option cost?
paragraphs: At Artecium, websites start at €750 (Essential) and the Professional plan costs €1,500. Projects with advanced features — integrations, automation, multi-language — fall under the Business plan from €2,500.
Web applications start at €3,500 because they involve backend, database, authentication, security and specific business logic. Each application is quoted individually based on requirements.

If the project combines a public website with advanced features, it's worth assessing whether an expanded Business website solves it or whether a dedicated application is needed — the answer depends on concrete requirements.

sections.title: Checklist to decide
sections.intro: Answer these questions to understand what type of project you need.
items: Do visitors need to log in to access content or features?
Is there business logic that processes data (orders, bookings, calculations)?
Does the internal team need a dashboard or management tool?
Does the system need its own database with user data?
Is the main goal to inform and capture contacts, or to execute a process?
Do you need complex integrations with APIs, payments or external systems?

items.question: Can I start with a website and evolve to an app?
items.answer: Yes, and it's a common approach. Many clients start with a professional website and, as the business grows, develop a web application for features the site doesn't cover. Planning that evolution from the start helps avoid rework.

items.question: Is a website with a restricted area a web application?
items.answer: It depends on complexity. A simple restricted area (documents, basic profile) can be part of a Business website. A portal with multiple features, roles and business logic is a web application.

items.question: How much does a web application cost at Artecium?
items.answer: Web applications start at €3,500. The final price depends on functional requirements, integrations, security and usage volume. Each project is quoted individually after scope analysis.

items.question: WordPress or custom web application?
items.answer: WordPress and similar CMS platforms handle websites and blogs very well. When business logic is specific, integrations are complex or performance and security require full control, a custom web application makes more sense.

items.question: Do AI and automation fit in a website or app?
items.answer: Both. Chatbots and smart forms can integrate into a website (AI solutions from €750). Complex process automation (from €1,500) can link website, CRM and internal tools — sometimes in a dedicated web application.

hero.title: AI-powered website — what changes in practice?
hero.intro: Artificial intelligence is no longer science fiction — it's available to businesses of any size. On a website, AI and automation can qualify leads, answer frequently asked questions, process forms and connect tools without constant manual intervention. We explain what's possible, what it costs and when it makes sense.

sections.title: What does "AI-powered website" mean?
paragraphs: An AI-powered website isn't a site that "thinks for itself" — it's a site where intelligent components support concrete processes: responding to visitors, qualifying contacts, generating content or automating flows between the website and other tools.

In practice, this translates to chatbots that respond based on site content, forms that adapt questions based on answers, assistants that route requests to the right team or automations that turn a contact into an organised lead in the CRM.
AI on a website works best with clear rules, human supervision when needed and integration with processes the company already uses.

sections.title: Concrete use cases
sections.intro: These are real applications of AI and automation on websites — not theoretical concepts.

items.title: Website chatbot
items.description: Answers frequently asked questions based on site content, collects contact information and routes complex requests to a human.

items.title: Smart forms
items.description: Adapt questions based on previous answers, qualify leads automatically and reduce unnecessarily long forms.

items.title: Automatic lead qualification
items.description: A visitor fills in the form → information is classified → the team receives only relevant leads with context.

items.title: Post-contact automation
items.description: Contact received → automatic confirmation email → CRM entry → team notification — without copying data manually.

items.title: Assisted content generation
items.description: Support for creating blog copy, service descriptions or client responses, with human review.

sections.title: Benefits for businesses
sections.intro: AI and automation on a website solve concrete operational problems — not just "innovation".
items: Less time on repetitive tasks (answering the same questions, copying data between systems)
Faster response to visitors — even outside business hours
Better qualified leads reach the team with context
Consistent processes — fewer human errors in information transfer
Scalability — the website handles more contacts without proportionally increasing team size

plans.description: Chatbots, AI assistants, smart forms, content generation and lead qualification.

plans.name: Automation

plans.name: Business Automation
plans.description: AI agents, internal systems, complex integrations and tailored advanced automation.

sections.title: AI vs automation — which do you need?
paragraphs: Automation executes predefined tasks based on rules: "when a form arrives, send email and log in CRM". It doesn't interpret — it follows instructions.
AI can interpret information, generate responses or make decisions within defined limits: "when the visitor asks X, respond based on site content or route to a human".
Many projects combine both. A chatbot (AI) qualifies the visitor; an automation logs the contact in the CRM and notifies the team. The right combination depends on the process you want to improve.

sections.title: Where to start
paragraphs: The first step isn't choosing technology — it's identifying the process that consumes the most time or where contacts are lost. Manually answering the same questions? Copying form data to the CRM? Slow to respond to contact requests?

A professional website (from €750) with a basic chatbot or smart form (AI Solutions from €750) can be an accessible starting point. More complex automation (from €1,500) makes sense when multiple tools are involved or processes have several steps.
If the project combines a new website with AI and automation, it's worth planning everything together — integration is more efficient when designed from the start.

items.answer: Yes. Chatbots, smart forms and automations can integrate into existing websites, provided the platform allows it technically. Feasibility is assessed during the project discovery phase.

items.answer: No. AI and automation reduce repetitive tasks and improve response speed — but important processes benefit from human supervision. Automation routes to a person when the case requires it.
